one_liner: Complete CSV of all 30,000+ active GSA Multiple Award Schedule (MAS) contract holders with company name, UEI, schedule type, NAICS codes, and socioeconomic certifications — the same data GovTribe and Bloomberg Government charge $3,000–$15,000/year to access
audience: Government contracting consultants prospecting for GSA Schedule application clients (typical engagement: $5,000–$50,000), subcontractors building teaming partner databases of primes in complementary NAICS codes, and B2B service vendors (payroll, insurance, HR software, recruiting) targeting federal contractors who represent 20-40% higher LTV than commercial SMBs due to contract stability and compliance-driven spending. Solo GovCon coaches need this to identify companies selling federally without GSA Schedules (ideal conversion prospects), while small 8(a) and SDVOSB firms use it to find large primes seeking diverse teaming partners for set-aside contracts. Regional matchmaking platforms like Winvale charge $200–$500/month for similar prime contractor databases — this delivers the full TAM as a one-time CSV at 1/3 the cost of a single month's subscription.
format_rationale: CSV is the universal format for CRM upload (Salesforce, HubSpot, Pipedrive), filtering by state/NAICS/socioeconomic status in Excel or Google Sheets, and cross-referencing against SAM.gov registrations to identify federal sellers who lack GSA Schedules. GovCon consultants need to segment by business size and schedule type to prioritize outreach (small businesses new to IT Schedule 70 are highest-intent prospects for consulting services), while subcontractors filter by location and NAICS to build geographically relevant teaming partner lists. B2B vendors import directly into marketing automation platforms to launch campaigns targeting federal contractors in specific industries (e.g., 'all IT Schedule 70 holders in the Mid-Atlantic with <500 employees'). A static CSV prevents ongoing subscription lock-in — buyers pay once, filter repeatedly, and own the data permanently for their specific use case.

At $79, a single Gumroad sale to a solo GovCon coach or small subcontractor covers the product development cost multiple times over, and the absence of any flat-file competitor below $1,000 leaves massive pricing headroom.

Pre-built Excel filter formulas to segment the database by industry vertical — instant lists of 'all IT services schedule holders' (NAICS 541511, 541512, 541519), 'all facilities maintenance contractors' (NAICS 561210, 561720), 'all professional services firms' (NAICS 541611, 541618, 541690) — saves 30 minutes of manual filtering and prevents NAICS code lookup errors

One free annual CSV refresh delivered via email for 3 years (2027, 2028, 2029 editions) — GSA Schedules are renewed annually and new companies win contracts quarterly, so the database becomes stale within 12 months; lifetime updates ensure GovCon consultants always have current prospect data without repurchasing, massively increasing perceived value vs. the $79 one-time price and creating competitive moat vs. enterprise SaaS platforms that gate updates behind $3K/year paywalls

core_fields: Unique Entity ID (UEI, 12-character alphanumeric replacing DUNS)
Schedule name and category (IT Schedule 70, Professional Services, Facilities Maintenance MAS, etc.)
Special Item Numbers (SINs) authorized under schedule
NAICS codes offered under the contract
Contract period of performance (award date, current expiration)
Business size classification (small business flag per FAR 19.001)
Socioeconomic designations (8(a), HUBZone, WOSB, VOSB, SDVOSB)
Primary contract contact (name, phone, email where publicly available)
estimated_row_count_rationale: GSA reports approximately 30,000 active Multiple Award Schedule contracts as of 2025, representing $35+ billion in annual federal procurement spend across 20,000–25,000 unique companies (some hold multiple schedule types). One row per active contract — vertically integrated firms holding both IT Schedule 70 and Professional Services schedules appear as separate records. Target output includes only active contracts (exclude expired, closed, or terminated schedules) to ensure all records represent currently qualified federal contractors.
source_url_rationale: GSA eLibrary is the official, authoritative public database of all GSA Schedule contracts, maintained by the General Services Administration and updated weekly. Data is 100% public domain per FAR 9.105-2(b)(1) and freely downloadable as Excel or CSV with no authentication required. All contract metadata (company name, UEI, schedule type, SINs, NAICS, socioeconomic certifications) is disclosed under federal procurement transparency regulations. Zero PII — all data is company-level business information. No web scraping required; direct bulk export available, making this a low-engineering-lift, zero-legal-risk data product.

engineering_notes: Direct bulk download from GSA eLibrary at https://www.gsaelibrary.gsa.gov/ — no web scraping required. Export available as Excel or CSV. Normalize schedule name variations (e.g., 'IT Schedule 70' vs. 'Information Technology Schedule 70' vs. 'Schedule 70'). Deduplicate by contract number (primary key). Geocode city/state to standardize location data. Flag records missing UEI or CAGE code (rare but possible for very old contracts grandfathered before 2022 UEI transition). Validate socioeconomic certification flags against SBA.gov databases where possible to catch stale certifications. Scope to active contracts only — filter out expired/closed/terminated status. Estimated engineering time: 8–12 hours (low complexity, direct download source, minimal transformation).
compliance_notes: Zero PII — all data is company-level business information (legal entity names, contract numbers, business addresses, socioeconomic certifications). GSA Schedule contract holder information is 100% public per FAR 9.105-2(b)(1) and federal procurement transparency statutes. No authentication required to access source data. No terms of service restrictions on redistribution (government data in public domain). Contact information (phone, email) is publicly listed by contractors themselves in GSA eLibrary for business development purposes — no privacy concerns. No GDPR applicability (US government contractors, not EU individuals). Automatic PASS expected from compliance-officer.
competitive_moat: Only flat-file CSV option under $1,000 — all competitors (GovTribe, BGOV, Winvale) sell annual subscriptions starting at $200/month, not one-time data exports. 'Own it forever' positioning vs. subscription lock-in. Bonus stack (especially lifetime annual updates for 3 years) delivers enterprise-grade value at impulse-buy pricing. SEO advantage on 'GSA Schedule holders CSV', 'federal contractor database download', 'teaming partner list' — zero Gumroad competition in this niche.
